title: ATOMS: ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of massive Star-forming regions - XX. Probability distribution function of integrated intensity for dense molecular gas tracers
question: Investigate the correlation between gravitationally bound gas and star formation by analyzing integrated intensity probability distribution functions (I-PDFs) and power-law tails of dense molecular gas tracers across massive star-forming clumps.

what.value: Global dust temperature, clump mass, bolometric luminosity, distance, and radius of target clumps

evidence.quote: The global dust temperature, mass, and luminosity of these 146 targets were obtained from the infared spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting (Faúndez et al. 2004; Urquhart et al. 2018), and are categorized in Table A1 of Liu et al. (2020a).
The volume area is c' [2], where R (compiled by Liu et al. 2020a) is the radius of the clump.

external_data.citation: Faúndez et al. (2004); Urquhart et al. (2018); Liu et al. (2020a)

what.value: [12C]/[13C] abundance ratio as a function of Galactocentric distance

evidence.loc: 3.2 The L bol -L mol scaling relations
evidence.quote: We assummed the abundance ratio X 12 /X 13 =[HCO [+] ]/[H [13] CO [+] ] as a function of Galactocentric distance as given by Pineda et al. (2013),

recipe.goal: Smooth images to uniform linear resolution within distance intervals and generate integrated intensity maps
recipe.method: Divide 135 sources into three distance intervals (<3 kpc, 3-6 kpc, >6 kpc), smooth within each interval using CASA to uniform linear resolution, and produce integrated intensity maps for the six molecular transitions.
key_parameters: Linear resolutions: 0.03 kpc (< 3 kpc), 0.07 kpc (3 to 6 kpc), 0.15 kpc (> 6 kpc)

recipe.goal: Construct and fit integrated intensity probability distribution functions (I-PDFs)
recipe.method: Fit the lower-intensity side of the I-PDF peak with a log-normal distribution, subtract the best-fit log-normal profile from the overall I-PDF, and fit the remaining high-intensity component with a linear regression power-law fit.
assumptions: I-PDF is composed of a log-normal distribution at low intensity and a power-law tail at high intensity.

recipe.goal: Calculate power-law tail molecular line luminosities and fit L_bol - L_mol(p) scaling relations
recipe.method: Calculate molecular line luminosity for the power-law high-intensity component L_mol(p) from velocity-integrated flux, line frequency, and distance, then fit L_bol vs L_mol(p) scaling relations in log-log space.

recipe.goal: Estimate optical depths of HCO+, H13CO+, HCN, and H13CN
recipe.method: Measure average brightness temperature within a 30 arcsec circular aperture centered on each source and solve the brightness temperature ratio equation between main and 13C isotopologue lines.
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and identical excitation temperature for main and isotopologue lines
Beam-filling factor = 1 and cosmic background temperature T_bg = 2.73 K

recipe.goal: Analyze correlations of I-PDF power-law slope s and equivalent density profile exponent alpha with clump properties and star formation efficiency
recipe.method: Examine power-law slope s against L/M and clump surface density; convert H13CO+ slope s into radial density profile exponents for spheres and filaments; compute Spearman rank correlation coefficients and linear fits with R^2 between L_bol/L_mol(p) and s or alpha.
key_parameters: Outlier rejection for alpha_c > 2.5 (3 points excluded)
assumptions: H13CO+ is optically thin so intensity is directly proportional to column density

score_reason: Public ALMA project code (2019.1.00685.S) and clear high-level analytical equations (line luminosity, optical depth, density exponent conversion), plus online supplementary tables, but missing low-level parameters for moment-0 integration ranges and the exact I-PDF log-normal/power-law separation algorithm.
